backtest_protocol: docs/backtesting.md canonical three fixed windows. Core uses canonical snapshots; Space variants use exp-20260510-028 augmented Space snapshots. The accepted_before variant reproduces exp-20260512-032 policy semantics.
decision_rationale: The space_data_defense theme-segment risk scalar did not clear the three-window gate on top of exp-20260512-032. Do not retry adjacent Space data/defense theme scalar values on these frozen snapshots; the next Space edge needs forward catalyst replacement value or a different production-observable catalyst-quality field.

gate1.known_bias: Space candidate snapshots are frozen historical replay copies built from a 2026-05-10 research universe; any accepted change must remain default-off metadata until forward evidence matures.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: risk allocation: scale only official Space signals whose universe-registry theme_segment is space_data_defense.

2_history_check.exp-20260511-111: Rejected PL/BKSY data-vendor trend target widening; this tests a broader production registry bucket, not target width.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-014/015/016/019/021: Rejected peer-trend, 52w, breadth, R/R, and breakout volume refinements; those variables stay fixed.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-023: Rejected GSAT candidate-pool expansion; no ticker expansion in this test.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-032: Accepted launch/lunar 1.10x theme-segment scalar; this is the fixed before state.

gate_questions.3_single_causal_variable: space_data_defense_theme_segment_risk_scalar. Candidate pool, accepted Space risk scalars, targets, stops, ranking, add-ons, LLM/news, and live slots stay fixed.
gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: docs/backtesting.md three fixed windows; require positive aggregate EV/PnL, at least 2/3 improved EV windows, no EV-regressed window, max drawdown drift <= 0.5 pp, survival >= 5%, >=50 total trades, and nonzero adjusted data/defense signals.
gate_questions.5_reproducibility: This script reruns core, accepted exp-20260512-032 Space stack, and each data/defense theme-segment scalar across the canonical augmented Space snapshots.

hypothesis: After launch/lunar, TQS, peer-breakout, and IWM-relative Space risk allocation were accepted, the remaining production-visible candidate-quality question is whether the PL/BKSY/RDW data/defense bucket deserves a separate risk budget. This avoids LLM soft-ranking because the forward event-state sample is still too thin, and it does not add noisy tickers.
